Dark Retro Webpage turns the late-1990s and early-2000s internet aesthetic up to full volume — pixel typography, Winamp-era UI flourishes, and a dark palette that recalls screen-glow in a dim bedroom. This is an unabashedly personal site, built for developers who want their portfolio to declare a point of view the moment the page loads.

## Theme Overview

Dark Retro Webpage inhabits the moody, late-internet era between the mid-1990s and early 2000s — a moment when personal sites were starting to get darker, more stylized, and more self-aware. The design draws on pixel-art typography, Winamp-inspired panel details, dark background tones, and the kind of layered UI decoration that was everywhere in that era. The result is a portfolio that feels less like a professional document and more like a carefully curated personal space: opinionated, atmospheric, and completely itself. Every design choice here is deliberate and unapologetic.

## Design Highlights

- Dark, screen-glow palette rooted in late-1990s and early-2000s personal site culture
- Pixel typography that references bitmap screen fonts of the era
- Winamp-inspired UI details including panel accents and compact interface elements
- Layered decorative elements typical of the high-personality personal sites of the period
- A strong, opinionated visual identity that rewards visitors who share the cultural reference

## Who This Theme Suits

Dark Retro Webpage is made for developers who grew up online in the late 1990s or early 2000s and want their portfolio to speak that language — people who customized their Winamp skins, had a LiveJournal, and remember when having a personal domain was genuinely cool. It suits front-end developers, designers, and digital artists whose work carries a strong personal aesthetic and who want their portfolio to reflect that with confidence.

<Note>
  Dark Retro Webpage's pixel typography and dark palette work best when your project screenshots and visual content also lean into high-contrast or stylized aesthetics.
</Note>
